To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the coupling of an activity specific model with an automatic activity and posture recognition algorithm improves PAEE and EE predictions from accelerometry.
the automatic recognition of activities performed and their coupling with an activity specific energy expenditure model improves energy expenditure prediction from triaxial accelerometers.

the coupling of a simple linear model to an automatic activity recognition (AAR model, which is a simple linear model coupled to an automatic activity/postural recognition algorithm) improves the accuracy of the predictions of physical activity energy expenditures (PAEE) from hip worn tri-axial accelerometry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of triaxial accelerometers to measure energy expenditure.
the development and validation of an activity specific model for the assessment of PAEE from triaxial accelerometers, which is coupled with an automatic recognition algorithm.
the development of a model that improves the accuracy of physical activity (PA), and energy expenditure (EE).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AAR model improved the variance explained in PAEE and T EE predictions from accelerometry compared to the Freedson model.

the AAR model is a promising tool to estimate physical activity and energy expenditure from accelerometry counts, but further validation is needed to confirm the findings in different population and activity contexts.

the model proposed in this paper, which couples the activity specific regression model with an automatic recognition of the performed activities, improves the accuracy and precision of the PAEE prediction from triaxial accelerometric data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a model coupling an activity specific model with an activity recognition algorithm improved physical activity energy expenditure and total energy expenditure predictions from a triaxial accelerometer.

the coupling between a simple automatic activity recognition algorithm and an activity specific count-based model improves the accuracy of PAEE and total energy expenditure predictions from hip worn tri-axial accelerometry in free living conditions.

the coupling of a model based on accelerometry counts and an automatic activity recognition improves the precision and accuracy of the predictions for PAEE from accelerometers in free living conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a model coupling an AAR algorithm with an activity count based model improves the prediction of PAEE and TEEE from a hip worn accelerometry device.

automatic activity recognition algorithms, coupled with activity specific count based models, may help improve the precision of physical activity and energy expenditure estimates from accelerometry in free living conditions.
the precision of accelerometry based PAEE predictions can be improved using a model that accounts for the nature of performed activities, which is not currently done by the most used algorithms.
